new.v: Old river channel, ford and lakeshore ground
new.st: North of Mankato, the river of the 1850s wound in tight loops 400-600 m west of today's straight channel. The land inside and along those old loops was riverbank when the Dakota and the first settlers used it, and it's dry floodplain now.
new.t: Old cutbanks and point bars are where river-dropped coins and trade goods settle. Work the edge of the old channel, which shows as a low swale on LiDAR. North Mankato side. Access: Nicollet County land, owner not checked (parcel host blocked). Ask before going on.

new.v: Old river channel, ford and lakeshore ground
new.st: The oldest mapped crossing of the Blue Earth: the wagon trail from South Bend to Mankato forded it here, by the Le Hillier town site and the Fort L'Huillier marker. The mill dam just downstream was one of the first in the county. Unconfirmed, one source.
new.t: Fords scatter dropped coins, buckles and wagon iron along both approaches. Work the banks above high water. Access: W bank private residential (N Sturgis St); E bank no parcel (river/levee land). Ask first.

new.st: A lake of the 1850s, now gone, that sat in the old Le Sueur riverbed on Mankato's south side. Lakeshores like this were camp spots.
new.t: Look for the old shoreline terrace around the low ground. Access: City of Mankato land (38 + 48 ac), likely the Rasmussen Woods area. City permission needed, or look only.

bec-jefferson-bend-1908.st: the 1850s land-survey plat draws the loop, a westward bend through sec 1 T108N R27W that reaches 44.1863,-94.0202, right where Hiniker Pond is now. Today's river runs about 800 m east of the loop's tip.

bec-jones-ford.st: in the 1850s the trails met the river at the sec 23/26 line (44.1373,-94.040), where an east-bank trail along the bluff and a west-bank road toward the Jones land in sec 27 reach the river. That is a second candidate for the ford, about 1.6 km NE of the 1950s bridge pin.
